observations: Photo 0: a bare 4-cylinder car engine sitting on a metal rack, timing belt and pulleys visible, no engine code or manufacturer badge legible anywhere on the block or valve cover.
Photo 0: wiring harness connectors dangling, no visible leaks, cracks, or corrosion on visible surfaces, but underside and rear of block not shown.
Photo 1: a starter motor (and possibly an alternator) sitting on top of a larger plastic-wrapped part, with a watermark reading 'PROMISE AUTO VENTURES'.
Photo 1: no part numbers, brand stampings, or vehicle fitment labels are legible on the starter or the wrapped item beneath it.
No odometer, compression tester, dyno screen, or start-up video is shown for either item.

identity.kind: used car engine (photo 0) and used starter motor (photo 1)

claims.evidence: No import documents, customs sticker, or Korean-market badge is visible in either photo; origin cannot be confirmed from images alone.
No start-up video, compression test, or bench test clip provided for either part.

risks.risk: Engine may not run or may have internal damage (cracked block, worn bearings, seized components).
risks.proof: Video of the engine cranking and running, plus a compression test reading.

risks.risk: Vehicle application (make/model/year) for the engine and starter is unknown, which is the main price driver for used Korean engine parts.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the engine ID/stamped code plate and the starter's part number tag.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced without knowing fitment; treated as unidentified generic engine/starter

risks.risk: Starter motor may be faulty or mismatched to the engine shown.
risks.proof: Bench test video of the starter spinning under load.

risks.risk: Hidden damage to engine underside, oil pan, or rear seal not shown in the single angle provided.
risks.proof: Additional photos from the side, rear, and underside of the block.

risks.risk: Mileage and prior accident/flood history unverifiable.
risks.proof: Photo of any accompanying paperwork, mileage sticker, or import tag.

proof_requests: Photo of the engine's stamped ID/code plate (usually on the block near the bellhousing or front face).
Video of the engine cranking and idling.
Photo of the starter motor's part number/tag.
Bench test video of the starter motor.
Seller's statement of exact vehicle make, model, and year these parts are pulled from.
response.reason: Neither the engine nor the starter carries a legible brand, model, or vehicle-fitment marking in the photos, and fitment is the primary price driver for used Korean engine parts; without it, even a worst-case price bracket cannot be set.
